newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso Q1 falls, beats forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Enso Q1 falls, beats forecasts.

text.p: Enso Group, to be Europe's second largest forestry firm after a German acquisition, on Tuesday reported first quarter profit down 28 percent but above market expectations, and forecast a steady full-year showing.

Reporting profit after financial items down to 480 million markka ($94 million) from 668 million in the year-ago period, Enso's profit was above the highest analysts' forecast at 470 million markka and clearly overshot the median at 351 million markka.

Echoing the caution of its compatriot rival UPM-Kymmene, Europe's largest forestry firm, Enso said it expected full-year 1997 earnings to be similar to 1996, when it made a 1.7 billion markka profit after financial items.

"The strengthening of short-fibre market pulp prices in the past few weeks will make it easier to raise paper prices. Prices are expected to rise during the second half of the year," it said in a statement.
This was Enso's first quarterly report, shifting from four-monthly interims, and proforma figures were not made available ahead of the news.
Its net financial costs showed a dramatic fall to 199 million markka from 325 million in the year-ago period.
Earnings per share fell sharply to 1.36 markka from 2.06 markka: net sales slipped to 6.5 billion from 6.7 billion.
Enso repeated its earnings and cash flow would be boosted by its acquisition this year of 50.4 percent of German paper-maker E. Holtzmann & Cie AG for 1.8 billion markka.
"The deal will improve the group's per-share cash flow immediately and earnings per share as the synergy benefits materialise," Enso said.
It said its majority Holtzmann holding was consolidated on April 28.
